sections.html:
Mobile is the county seat of Mobile County, at the head of Mobile Bay on Alabama's Gulf Coast. It is the state's only deep water port city, and the second largest in population after Huntsville.

The city covers 180.07 square miles, and 22.5 percent of that is water. Elevation runs from 10 feet on Water Street downtown to 211 feet at the Mobile Regional Airport. That range matters for flood risk, since low areas near the water behave very differently from the higher ground west of downtown.

  • Founded in 1702 by the Le Moyne brothers
  • Incorporated as a city on December 17, 1819
  • Nicknamed the Port City and the Azalea City
  • Home of the oldest organized Carnival in the United States

sections.h2: How many people live in Mobile?
sections.html:
Mobile had 187,041 residents in the 2020 census, and an annexation of land west of the city in July 2023 lifted the count to 204,689. The 2025 Census Bureau estimate is 200,824.

The city shrank for decades after peaking in 1960, and annexation has reversed that. The 2020 census counted 77,772 households, a median age of 37.3 and 17.3 percent of residents 65 or older.

sections.h2: What are the major employers in Mobile?
sections.html:
The University of South Alabama is Mobile's largest employer, with 11,500 people, followed by the Mobile County Public School System at 7,200. These figures come from the city's 2024 financial report as listed on Wikipedia.

Airbus opened its first United States A320 family assembly plant in Mobile in 2015 and added the A220 in 2019. The Mobile Aeroplex at Brookley covers 1,650 acres with more than 70 companies. The Port of Mobile ranks as the 12th largest port in the nation.

sections.h2: What does Mobile weather mean for a house?
sections.html:
Mobile is the wettest city in the contiguous 48 states in a 2007 study, with 66.3 inches of average annual rainfall. Hurricanes, storm surge and tornadoes are part of its history, so sellers often deal with roof, flood and water damage questions.

  • Hurricane Frederic, Category 3, struck on September 12, 1979
  • Hurricane Katrina brought an 11.45 foot storm surge in 2005
  • Hurricane Sally hit in 2020, followed a month later by Zeta, a Category 3
  • A December 25, 2012 tornado damaged at least 100 structures in Midtown

Heavy rain and humidity also feed mold and rot in older homes. A buyer's inspection will look closely at roofs, crawl spaces and drainage. A cash buyer can price those findings in without waiting on a lender's repair demands.

sections.h2: Which Mobile neighborhoods have historic character?
sections.html:
Mobile's historic neighborhoods include Ashland Place, Campground, Church Street East, De Tonti Square, Leinkauf, Lower Dauphin Street, Midtown, Oakleigh Garden, Old Dauphin Way, Spring Hill and Toulminville. Home styles there include shotgun houses, Colonial Revival, Tudor Revival and Spanish Colonial Revival.

Older houses in these areas can have original wood windows, old wiring and settled foundations. Owners considering a sale should ask whether a district review applies to exterior work, which the city planning office can answer.

sections.h2: How do property taxes work for a Mobile sale?
sections.html:
The Mobile County Revenue Commission handles property tax and notes that its offices are closed on Wednesdays. Statewide, Alabama property taxes are due October 1 and are delinquent after December 31.

If you sell mid year, the title company normally splits the bill between buyer and seller. Because a bill follows the owner of record, a seller should confirm the current year's tax is accounted for in the closing statement.

The state recording tax on a deed is 50 cents per $500 of value under Alabama Code 40-22-1, with proof of the actual price filed with the deed.

sections.h2: How does Mardi Gras shape Mobile?
sections.html:
Mobile claims the oldest organized Carnival celebration in the United States, rooted in the French Creole population of the early 1700s. In 1830 the city saw the first organized Carnival mystic society parade in the country.

That culture is tied to downtown streets such as Dauphin Street, where many 1800s storefronts still stand. Sellers near downtown may want to plan showings around the Carnival calendar.

sections.h2: What are the main industries in Mobile besides the port?
sections.html:
Aerospace, steel, shipbuilding, retail, services, construction, medicine and manufacturing are the major industries in Mobile. Austal USA was founded in 1999 and expanded its aluminum shipbuilding on Blakeley Island in 2005.

BAE Systems Southeast Shipyards operates the former Alabama Drydock site on Pinto Island and employs about 600 workers. In 2005 the Alabama State Docks finished the largest expansion in its history, a project costing over $300 million.

sections.h2: Can snow and heavy rain hurt a Mobile house?
sections.html:
Yes. Mobile averages 120 days a year with measurable rain, and snow, though rare, struck on January 21, 2025 with accumulations up to 8.5 inches and near blizzard conditions. Pipes and roofs built for a mild climate can be strained by an event like that.

No snow fell in the city from 1996 to 2017.

sections.h2: What do 2020 census figures show about Mobile households and residents?
sections.html:
Mobile had 77,772 households in the 2020 census, and 45,953 of them were families. About 27.7 percent of households had children under 18 and 21.9 percent of residents were under 18.

For every 100 women there were 87.4 men. The city is majority Black or African American, at 51.06 percent of the 2020 count, and 40.12 percent of residents were non Hispanic white. After the 2023 annexation, Wikipedia notes Mobile became a majority minority city.

For a seller, the practical point is that neighborhoods differ widely in age, ownership and housing type across 139 square miles of land, so the value of a house depends heavily on its exact location.

sections.h2: What colleges and hospitals are in Mobile?
sections.html:
The University of South Alabama is the city's top employer, and Infirmary Health Systems, Springhill Medical Center and AltaPointe also rank among the ten largest. Spring Hill College is another local institution, and it accepted students of all races in the 1950s.

Medical and university jobs bring steady turnover of staff, residents and students, and some households sell quickly when a contract ends or a new position starts elsewhere.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work in Mobile?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Mobile starts with an offer, then a title search, then a signed contract and a closing at a title or law office. The deed is recorded afterward and the tax is paid on recording.

  • Reasons owners sell: storm damage, inheritance, tenants, or a move
  • Title work still applies to every sale
  • Flood zone and insurance history matter to many buyers
  • Repairs can be left to the buyer

Since the city had a major annexation in 2023, confirm that the parcel is inside city limits when you check taxes and services.

faqs.q: What is the population of Mobile, AL?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 200,824 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 187,041, and a 2023 annexation added land west of the city.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Mobile, Alabama?
faqs.a: October 1, and they are delinquent after December 31, per the Alabama Department of Revenue.

faqs.q: Is Mobile at risk from hurricanes?
faqs.a: Yes. Frederic in 1979, Katrina in 2005, Sally and Zeta in 2020 all affected the city. Storm surge and wind damage are common reasons for repairs before a sale.

faqs.q: What is the largest employer in Mobile?
faqs.a: The University of South Alabama, with 11,500 employees listed in the city's 2024 financial report.

faqs.q: What is the Alabama deed tax?
faqs.a: Fifty cents for each $500 of value conveyed, under Alabama Code 40-22-1.

faqs.q: Can I sell a storm damaged house in Mobile?
faqs.a: Yes. Sellers can sell as-is to a buyer who accepts the condition. Disclose known damage and settle the title and tax items before closing.
